Perfume rating 4.11 out of 5 with 8,368 votes

Angel Muse by Mugler is a Oriental Vanilla fragrance for women. Angel Muse was launched in 2016. The nose behind this fragrance is Quentin Bisch. Top notes are Pink Pepper and Grapefruit; middle note is Hazelnut cocoa spread; base notes are Patchouli and Vetiver.

In April 2016, Thierry Mugler will launch the latest addition to the famous gourmand, Angel, the "futuristic - gourmet" Angel Muse. As Angel from 1992 represented the first gourmand perfume, so is the new edition announced as the first gourmand scent of vetiver for women.

“New fragrance, new bottle, new codes: a shock wave is shaking up the Angel galaxy. Angel MUSE, the new Eau de Parfum you will hate to love.”

Angel Muse is here to renew the style of the gourmand fragrance genre. Its accord is luminous and not too sweet; it gradually develops into an elegant gourmand to stimulate our "olfactory appetite". The composition is developed by Quentin Bisch, containing a sweet accord of hazelnut cream with the elegant, woody and typically masculine character of vetiver balancing the creamy sweetness.

“To make an analogy, you could say that Angel Eau de Parfum is the star, while Angel MUSE orbits around the star and revolves as if around a galaxy.” Christophe de Lataillade, Creative Director for MUGLER fragrances

The bottle design is described as a “cosmic pebble", made of an elliptical, silver, metal ring with gently ambery, nude glass in the middle which reportedly evokes the surface of Mars.

The face of the perfume is Georgia May Jagger, who followed the steps of her mother Jerry Hall as the face of the Angel perfume line. The photographer of the campaign is Sølve Sundsbø.

The fragrance is available as a 30 and 50 ml Eau de Parfum.

Marta_Serafina 11/20/25 23:44

My relationship with this fragrance, much like with the original Angel is a classic love/hate story. It’s a sweet scent with plenty of chocolate, but I wouldn’t call it a typical gourmand, as there’s a huge amount of patchouli and woody notes running through it. It’s a very distinctive, slightly quirky composition, definitely for those who enjoy bold fragrances. As much as I love stronger perfumes, I have to be in the right mood to wear this one, because the patchouli is so prominent that it can become tiring after a while. As with most Mugler perfumes, the longevity and projection are very good, although not quite as powerful as the original Angel. It’s definitely a fragrance for the autumn and winter season.

crimsonbutterflies 05/09/25 09:45

Discontinued—but never forgotten.

Some perfumes flirt with your senses. Angel Muse seduced mine.

From the moment I first tried it, I was completely captivated. This wasn’t just a perfume—it was an experience, a statement, a temptation in a bottle. I fell hard for it, and I never looked back.

Angel Muse was everything I craved in a fragrance: deep, sensual, and unapologetically bold. The patchouli in this scent was divine—earthy yet refined, intense yet elegant. It grounded the perfume with that unmistakable Mugler DNA, but Muse elevated it with a new, irresistible twist: a creamy, nutty hazelnut-cocoa accord that felt almost edible. Sweet, but never juvenile. Warm, but never dull. It was like the forbidden love child of chocolate and woodsmoke, wrapped in silk and sin.

What truly made me fall in love, though, was the longevity. This was no fleeting scent. Angel Muse clung to skin, hair, and fabric like a second skin. I would catch whispers of it on myself all day—sometimes even the next morning. It had that rare power to haunt a room without overpowering it, and to linger on scarves and sweaters like a memory you don’t want to let go of.

There was something magnetic about it—like you were wrapped in mystery, sensuality, and warmth. I wore it on cool evenings and always felt more confident, more alluring, more me. People noticed. I noticed. It made ordinary moments feel cinematic.

That’s why it broke my heart when it was discontinued.

Perfume lovers know: when a scent like this disappears, it feels like losing a piece of your past. Angel Muse wasn’t just a bottle on my dresser. It was a scent that marked seasons of my life, moods, even memories. I’ve been chasing that feeling ever since, but nothing has truly filled the void it left behind.

If you ever find a bottle—hold onto it. Cherish it. Because Angel Muse was a modern classic, and for those of us who loved it, it always will be.

Angel Muse does NOT smell like the "powdered Nutella" line that every reviewer on social media likes to regurgitate, which is why I didn't like this fragrance at first -- it was the unmet false expectations of a chocolate gourmand. Fortunately for Angel Muse, it is more than a linear chocolate note, which is what I like about it (after I approached the fragrance on its own merits).

To start, the notes are accurate. When you first spray this, you'll get a blast of Pink Pepper and Grapefruit in the top notes along with Patchouli. Once the perfume dries down, it becomes sweeter yet still not a linear chocolate. It almost reminds me of Kilian Angel's Share in a way, but unlike Angel's Share which smelled too literally like an apple cinnamon pie, Angel Muse smells like an actual perfume. So Muse is unique, mysterious, sweet, spicy, and alluring.

Now that Muse is discontinued, you'll likely have to blind buy it. I'd recommend doing so if you think you'll like it because there is nothing else that's similar on the market, and if you don't like it, you can easily resell it. But know in advance that Angel Muse is not a powdered Nutella gourmand, and I mean that in the best way.

Angel Muse is very very pretty. I do not recall anything "Angel" smelling this nice.

Opening is strong, heady patchouli bomb. If I push my nose to my skin and concentrate, I can detect a very small amount of cocoa, or chocolate. A HEAVENLY GOURMAND 💫

The original Angel is an incredible Gourmand that opens with notes of patchouli, vanilla (ethyl-vanillin), caramel, cotton candy (ethyl-maltol), chocolate and a host of other accords. However, Angel Muse Edp transforms this composition into something more "earthy", with a vetiver opening evoking smells of wood and earth.

Angel Muse definitely awakens my olfactory appetite, but unlike the original Angel, Muse presents itself as a Gourmand Vetiver. It's great!, right?... Vetiver being a commonly masculine note. When I smell it, honestly, I can't perceive the red fruits in its opening, but I do notice the pink pepper mixed with a soft touch of slightly bitter grapefruit and the exquisite hazelnut cream that reminds me of Nutella cream, but without sugar. Truly a delight!

It is worth clarifying that the similarity between Angel and Angel Muse does not lie in their sweetness, but in the structure of the perfume. In the opening there is a bright and fresh explosion of fruits, spices and citrus, with white flowers like jasmine and lily of the valley. All this florality is similar to Angel, especially in the patchouli, which is Angel's signature signature. This is followed by a magnificent and exquisite hazelnut-cocoa cream accord and finally a magnetic explosion with the elegant and woody character of vetiver. Infusing depth and warmth in the dry down phase.

In my opinion, Angel Muse Edp is one of the best flakers of the traditional Angel.

"Muse" has a warm, spicy, zesty and slightly bitter opening. The pepper and grapefruit combine surprisingly well. Although it is a completely different scent, "Gold" by Kim Kardashian has a somewhat similar opening due to the shared notes. The top notes last about 20 minutes then "Muse" develops into a strong nutty, delicious scent with a lot of patchouli. The hazelnut cocoa note is quote strong however it smells more like roasted nuts and less like cocoa. However, this is an advantage to me since I prefer less sweetness.

It is strong but very wearable if used sparingly. I find it amazing for cold weather since it makes me feel warm. The closest thing to an office friendly "Angel" fragrance. Aside from the opening, it remains feminine while being dark and deep.

TWINKLE TWINKLE LITTLE STAR

1) A Moose is is the world's tallest, largest and heaviest existant species of deer and the only species in the genus Alces. It is also the tallest, and the second-largest, in body mass, land animal in North America, after the American bison. "Moose" and "Muse" are non related names even if they sound the same.
2) A "Muse" is one of nine inspirational goddesses of literature, science, and the arts in Greek and Roman mythology.
3) "Muse" is an English rock band.
4) "The Muse" is a 1999 film directed by Albert Brooks.
5) "Muse" is a town on the Shweli River, Shan State, Myanmar.
6) Muse Watson (born in 1948) is an American actor.
7) M.U.S.E. - Mercer University School of Engineering, one of Mercer University's eleven colleges and schools.
8) MUSE, a brand name for Prostaglandin E1, an erectile dysfunction treatment.
9) MUSE, a 2026 proposed orbiter mission to the planet Uranus.
10) Angel Muse is a fragrance designed by Quentin Bisch for the French fashion company of Thierry Mugler.

Angel Muse EdP was announced in 2016 and is claimed to be the first gourmand vetiver for women. It reached the market as the first wave of renewal in the women's fragrance division of Thierry Mugler. I do not agree it to be a flanker of the original Angel. Angel Muse received the name of that famous pioneer perfume but represents a new page inside the Mugler book of feminine perfumes. Well... it's unisex for me.
It's a totally new product line in my opinion.
The presentation is very beautiful, drawing on a spatial and extra-terrestrial concept, and shining on any collector's shelf.

THE SCENT
Angel Muse is woody and incisive in the tradition of a unique Mugler gourmand fragrance. Thierry Mugler has proved that one can make modern perfumes without pepper and suggests a pink pepper vibe in the opening, but playing with a composition of red berries mixed with grapefruit notes. The grapefruit confers some citrus acidity, is unexpectedly not fruity, and gives a somewhat balanced impression.
The middle notes offer us a hazelnut cream heart with chocolate. Yes, it's a strong Nutella vibe that ends up characterizing the main olfactory chord of the fragrance.
The background accord houses two frequent notes but usually never in a combined form without moss, musk or wood. Mugler marries his signature note from the initial Angel - strong patchouli - with a remarkable woody and masculine vetiver. The prominent patchouli and hazelnut ensure the recognition of Mugler's DNA and appeal to many of his angelic followers. This combination suggests the aroma of caramel pudding and candies from a Luna Park, which we are already accustomed to with the Angel drydown.
Angel Muse is not a champion of performance, but his sillage remains high enough to provide enough projection to please even the casual Mugler brand faithful, and its longevity satisfies any suspicious critic.
Without any doubt, as in the Angel line of fragrances, Angel Muse is used as a perfume for the colder days and nights and gives a very high sexiness aura to its wearer. It is an excellent fragrance, worthy of succeeding or accompanying the long journey that the Angel can still have in the market. And it remains a somewhat unisex gimmick for many men who wear it. I personally like to apply it from time to time... like today.
Angel fanatics split up a bit between hugging or repelling this latest Mugler proposal. Angel Muse is neither too sweet nor too feminine which are two main features of the whole Angel family for ladies. This less sweet Muse blending suggests to us the masculine perfumes of the brand, the male Angels, and in particular, the A*Men perfume. If we put the Muse juice in a bottle of Pure Wood (just because of the colour), we can surely fool a lot of people with a fantastic new A*Men Pure Nutella.
Let's see the scoring of this sexy pink star:
___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___
- Opening: 8.5 (nice, seductive and cool with tangy notes of grapefruit and red berries; It prepares the way for the hazelnut cream heart, the perfume DNA in my opinion)
- Dry Down: 9.0 (vetiver intermingles with patchouli; very nice and alluring, but I would like it more intense)
- Longevity: 8.5 (3 good sprays may last up to 8 hours, maybe 9 hours)
- Sillage: 8.0 (up to 6 feet at its peak, 2~2.5 hours of projection, with 3 heavy sprays)
- Uniqueness: 9.0 (I don't claim to be an expert in feminine fragrances but, besides the original Angel and Flankers, and some of the Angel Men offer, I am not aware of any familiar fragrance. All the mentioned scents belong to the Mugler brand)
- Wearability: 8.0 (very easy to wear but avoid hot weather)
- Versatility: 8.5 ("all around" versatile feminine fragrance provided it's not a sweaty activity - consensual sex excluded; fantastic for a night out or clubbing; a bit cloying for the office or casual daily wear; I consider it as unisex)
- Compliments: 9.5 (This fragrance is a compliment magnet)
- Quality: 9.5 (Well above average quality, quality ingredients, nice flask, nice cap, nice sprayer)
- Presentation: 10.0 (no faults, beautiful, elegant, and nicer than the original Angel star shape)
- Price: 7.0 (50 ml non-tester for €41 on a FragranceX sale, but usually its similar to the original Angel price)
___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___
- Overall rating: 8.69/10.00
- between 7 and 8 =above average;
- between 8 and 9 = recommended;
- bigger than 9 = don't miss it;

My advice: If you still don't have it, just order it provided you are a Mugler fan. If not... it's better you try it before buying it. I do consider it a unisex perfume. I do have some masculine perfumes that smell more feminine than this one. The patchouli and the vetiver make a remarkable twist in this hazelnut and chocolate spread fragrance.
Recommended? Yes!

Music: Deep Purple - "Highway Star"

Carlitos 01/08/24 19:35

TWINKLE, TWINKLE LITTLE STAR

# A Muse is one of nine inspirational goddesses of literature, science, and the arts in Greek and Roman mythology.
# Muse is an English rock band.
# The Muse is a 1999 film directed by Albert Brooks.
# Muse is a town on the Shweli River, Shan State, Myanmar.
# Muse Watson (born in 1948) is an American actor.
# MUSE - Mercer University School of Engineering, one of Mercer University's eleven colleges and schools.
# MUSE, a brand name for Prostaglandin E1, an erectile dysfunction treatment.
# MUSE, a 2026 proposed orbiter mission to the planet Uranus.
# Angel Muse, a fragrance designed by Quentin Bisch for the French fashion company of Thierry Mugler.

Angel Muse EdP was announced in 2016 and is claimed to be the first gourmand vetiver for women. It reached the market as the first wave of renewal in the women's fragrance division of Thierry Mugler. I do not agree it is a flanker of the original Angel. Angel Muse received the name of that famous perfume but represents a new page inside the Mugler book of feminine perfumes (unisex for me). It's a totally new product line in my opinion.
The presentation is very beautiful, drawing on a spatial and extra-terrestrial concept, and shining on any collector's shelf.
Angel Muse is woody and incisive in the tradition of a unique MUGLER gourmand. Thierry Mugler has proved that one can make modern perfumes without pepper and suggests a pink pepper vibe in the opening, but playing with a composition of red berries mixed with grapefruit notes. The grapefruit confers some citrus acidity, is unexpectedly not fruity, and gives a somewhat balanced impression.
The middle notes offer us a hazelnut cream heart with chocolate. Yes, it's a strong Nutella vibe that ends up characterizing the main olfactory accord of the fragrance.
The background chord houses two frequent notes but usually never in a combined form without moss, musk or wood. Mugler marries his signature note from the initial Angel - strong patchouli - with a remarkable woody and masculine vetiver. The prominent patchouli and hazelnut ensure the recognition of Mugler's DNA and appeal to many of his angelic followers. This combination suggests the aroma of caramel pudding and candies from Luna Park, which we are already accustomed to with the Angel drydown.
Angel Muse is not a champion of performance, but his sillage remains high enough to provide enough projection to please even the casual Mugler brand faithful, and its longevity satisfies any suspicious critic.
Without any doubt, as in the Angel line of fragrances, Angel Muse is used as a perfume for the colder days and nights and gives a very high sexiness aura to its wearer. It is an excellent fragrance, worthy of succeeding or accompanying the long journey that the Angel can still have in the market. And it remains a somewhat unisex gimmick for many men who wear it. I personally like to apply it from time to time... like today.
Angel fanatics split up a bit between hugging or repelling this latest Mugler proposal. Angel Muse is neither too sweet nor too feminine which are two main features of the whole Angel family for ladies. This less sweet Muse blending suggests to us the masculine perfumes of the brand, the male Angels, and in particular, the A*Men perfume. If we put the Muse juice in a bottle of Pure Wood (just because of the colour), we can surely fool a lot of people with a fantastic new A*Men Pure Nutella.
Let's see the scoring of this sexy pink star:
___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___
- Opening: 8.5 (nice, seductive and cool with tangy notes of grapefruit and red berries; It prepares the way for the hazelnut cream heart, the perfume DNA in my opinion)
- DryDown: 9.0 (vetiver intermingles with patchouli; very nice and alluring, but I would like it more intense)
- Longevity: 8.5 (3 good sprays may last up to 8 hours, maybe 9 hours)
- Sillage: 8.0 (up to 6 feet at its peak, 2~2.5 hours of projection, with 3 heavy sprays)
- Uniqueness: 9.0 (I don't claim to be an expert in feminine fragrances but, besides the original Angel and Flankers, and some of the Angel Men offer, I am not aware of any familiar fragrance. All the mentioned scents belong to the Mugler brand)
- Wearability: 8.0 (very easy to wear but avoid hot weather)
- Versatility: 8.5 ("all around" versatile feminine fragrance provided it's not a sweaty activity - consensual sex excluded; fantastic for a night out or clubbing; a bit cloying for the office or casual daily wear; I consider it as unisex)
- Compliments: 9.5 (This fragrance is a compliment magnet)
- Quality: 9.5 (Well above average quality, quality ingredients, nice flask, nice cap, nice sprayer)
- Presentation: 10.0 (no faults, beautiful, elegant, and nicer than the original Angel star shape)
- Price: 7.0 (50 ml non-tester for €41 on a FragranceX sale, but its cost is usually similar to the regular Angel price)
___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___
- Overall rating: 8.69/10.00
- between 7 and 8 =above average;
- between 8 and 9 = recommended;
- bigger than 9 = don't miss it;

Advice: If you still don't have it, just order it provided you are a Mugler fan. If not... you should try it before buying it. I do consider it a unisex perfume. I do have some masculine perfumes that smell more feminine than this one. The patchouli and the vetiver make a remarkable twist in this hazelnut and chocolate spread fragrance.
Recommended? Yes!

Music: Deep Purple - "Highway Star"

Oh how I love Angel Muse!

We’re in the middle of summer right now, so of course it’s not the ideal temperature to wear it… But on some not-too-sunny days (like today)) I still spray it anyway and I adore it. My husband smelled it on me today and then kept coming back for more sniffs. I haven’t found another fragrance that has this effect on him.. So of course now this is discontinued. I’m really sad about it, but luckily my 50ml bottle is still pretty much full so I guess it will last quite a while.

While most fragrances perform very poorly on my skin, this (and other patchouli ones) are lasting quite a while. I’d say at least 7/8 hours, but sometimes even more. Sillage is also pretty good, my husband said he could smell it at arm length and got whiffs of the scents when I walked near him. This was with 3 sprays (one on each of my forearms and one on the back of my neck). I personally wouldn’t spray more because I think this could get headache inducing if over-sprayed and I definitely don’t want to suffocate anyone.

At first spray, the patchouli and pink pepper are all I can smell, which I personally love. Then, after maybe half an hour it turns sweeter and I get that Nutella smell everyone is talking about. Comforting, interesting and addictive.

Tony Balkan 03/19/23 23:02

The availability or unavailability of a fragrance in the store must not be confused for "in production" or "discontinued". A discontinued fragrance might still be available in the stores for months after it has been discontinued and a still in production one might be unavailable because it's out of stock, as in this case. Always check the brand's website to see the status of a fragrance. If it's discontinued, they remove it from the website long before it disappears from the stores.

ChocoLei 03/18/23 07:10

This is such a wonderful Angel flanker! I love it. I remember first trying it not too long after it was first launched, and I really got that Nutella accord, it was spot on-- I couldn't believe it. Fast forward to this year and I don't get the Nutella accord anymore, unfortunately--- I don't even get chocolate. However, it's still a great and unique scent.

The opening is amazing. Grapefruit and pink pepper are listed but I think the intent was to create a juicy, fresh pineapple accord because this is what I get! I made my 11-year old nephew smell it without giving him any piece of info about the notes. The first thing he spontaneously said: "This smells like pineapple!"
Pineapple can be a very tricky accord, as it can often leans in the soy sauce territory. This is not the case here, it smells so fresh and juicy.

Then I get the strong Angel DNA and its sweet, dark, enchanting patchouli. I wish I could get the hazelnut chocolate accord but I still love Angel Muse EDP very much. It pairs beautifully with Kayali Vanilla 28 and these two make a great combo for night outs. Angel Muse EDP also works great as a gourmand patchouli for more casual occasions in the day time, either on its own or paired with something more fun--- but it's definitely a cold weather and/or night scent as it's so potent and dense.

A great Mugler that I will cherish until the very last drop.

Absolutely love this ! Angel Muse is basically a more wearable Angel ! Not that Angel isn't wearable ,,, I love it , its controversial , talked about , wild , daring , crazy ,you name it !!!!
Angel muse is like the tamer version of it , more in the direction of innocent and sucree and Aqua chic .....BUT .....it's better ;)

Angel muse starts with a burst of patchouli and jammy zesty citrus fruits and red berries , almost like fresh version of the original Angel , same character , same face. Angel muse doesn't carry the same heaviness as Angel does , it's more of an airy cloud or a puff if that makes sense. Angel muse never becomes as sweet and as dense as Angel. After the initial angel shock has dried a little, the hazelnut cream appears , which is amazing to me. It's when I really start to love it. But it's not heavy sticky cream , it's light and airy , the rose helps to make it fresh rather than heavy ,,,At this point it's much lighter than angel with its heavy chocolate and caramel notes that can come across almost suede like ,,,, angel muse shines in the middle and as just mentioned the rose adds freshness and keeps it from being too heavy. It's the smell of sweet patchouli , rose with hazelnut cream , it's almost edible with a touch of saltiness , it's very much addictive ! The vetiver is a nice addition as it keeps it from boiling or flooding over the edge of über feminine ! Or in other words the vetiver combined with the patchouli gives it a slightly masculine touch in the same sense as angel EDT does with the cedar note.
I am impressed and will definitely get a second bottle once it arrives in my city !
For now I will treasure the one I have as it lays nicely on my dresser beside the blue Angel star. Like two comets from heaven !

Now I am in an angel craze again !

I know I'm screaming into a bag of bird seed, but Mugler should consider returning this complex yet wearable masterpiece back on the market, untouched, as-is. After all, the original Angel took years to gain popularity; wish they had that kind of faith today for Muse.

Truly, Muse remains the best Angel flanker (not to mention one of the best mass-market fragrances in 20 years) in a sea of uninspired ones.

Daria_21 08/11/16 06:55

Okay guys, I seriously need a chastity belt on my wallet!!! Just blind bought this yesterday, and literally the last thing I need is another fragrance, but the urge was too strong and so she came home with me :/

This perfume is sensational!! A very successful blind buy that I am honoured to own. I own the original Angel, and I don't find these two alike whatsoever. Other reviewers are correct - Angel Muse is a softer, more wearable flanker (not that Angel isn't wearable - I love it and wear it proudly!) This one is just more office appropriate, and can safely be sprayed a few times. I find Angel is max one spray and is most definitely a powerhouse of a frag. Muse is an all-season perfume, as it's not too strong, but certainly not too light, either.

Angel Muse is oh so smooth, creamy, rich and comforting. When I wear it, I instantly think of hot cocoa on a cold winter's day, snuggling up on the couch with my husband and son, with a fire crackling in the background. I'm really not great at discerning various notes, but to my nose, I get rich, warm, toasted hazelnuts, high quality milk chocolate drizzled over full fat whipped cream on a bed of even more toasted hazelnuts. I have no idea what vetiver smells like, but I guess it smells great because this is seriously working for me! I really don't smell any patchouli or grapefruit, and I'm not so sure about the pink pepper, either. I do smell a faint hint of rose, late in the glorious dry down. Indeed, it is soft, airy, almost cloud like - never heavy, cloying or offensive. My husband LOVES this one - usually I have to ask what he thinks of my perfume, but this morning he voluntarily said mmmm you smell incredible, wear that more often! Hold the phone, ladies!!!!

Longevity is generous - this baby goes throughout the day and night - when I wake up in the morning, albeit light, I can still smell this on my wrist, and it always seems a shame to wash it away in the shower. Sillage is moderate to heavy - a generous arm's length, with a beautiful trail left behind you. This perfume is also anything but linear - oh no, this juice takes you through various stages of amazingness, and there is not one stage that I don't love! The nutty accord is quite intriguing. I can't say I've smelled nuts in too many fragrances, but this one is bang on and so well done.

The bottle is unique - heavy, feels expensive, and yes, even futuristic! The only thing I don't like about Mugler's fragrances is that some of them don't stand up on their own. I wish they did! But that is such a minor detail; it's the juice inside that counts, after all.

If you're into sweet, airy, comforting gourmand fragrances, I can't see this disappointing you whatsoever. Such a beauty!

That's one of those fragrances that are somehow magnetic and repelling at the same time. To be honest, I haven't quite figured out yet its magic, but I only have been testing a tiny 2 ml bottle for a few days, so I might update my review later.

It's definitely sexy, but not in a vulgar kind of way. As an Alien fan for life (or so I thought), I was convinced that no matter what fragrance the "enemy" camp of Angels will come up with, nothing is going to change my alignment. I think this version of Angel, with its alluring hazelnut sweetness that is present but not in a suffocating kind of way (1 spray is more than enough), can easily make one a traitor. On me it doesn't have that much of a silage staying mostly close to skin, something I certainly appreciate in this fragrance. It would work the best and would reveal the best of its qualities in a nice cold (maybe even slightly frosty) winter, if you are lucky to have one. I wouldn't wear it in the office, but would be a perfect choice for a date in a nice restaurant, or for "walking in a winter wonderland", perhaps while checking out Christmas markets, tasting Gluhwein, and what not:)

Update: after 5 hours on my skin, I realized it smells very similar to Calvin Klein One Shock for Him, at least in its initial 2011 version.
